definition: To shorten a word, phrase, or text.
sentence: The teacher told me to abbreviate my twenty-page excuse, so I wrote, "Dog. Homework. Complicated."

definition: To help or encourage someone to do something wrong.
sentence: The dog abetted the cookie theft by barking whenever Mom approached the kitchen.

definition: To deliberately refrain from doing or consuming something.
sentence: I vowed to abstain from dessert, a noble commitment that survived until the waiter said "cheesecake."

definition: Existing as an idea rather than a concrete object; also a summary.
sentence: Justice is abstract; the Lego under my bare foot was painfully concrete.

definition: Extremely insulting, cruel, or harmful.
sentence: The parrot's abusive language was shocking, especially because Grandma claimed she had "no idea where he learned it."

definition: Easy to reach, use, understand, or obtain.
sentence: The cookies were technically accessible, assuming you had a ladder, lock picks, and no respect for household rules.

definition: An award or expression of praise.
sentence: My greatest accolade was a refrigerator magnet reading "World's Okayest Cook."

definition: To gather or increase gradually over time.
sentence: Dirty socks accumulated under my son's bed until they appeared to form their own municipal government.

definition: Sharpness of thought, perception, or senses.
sentence: Grandma's visual acuity is remarkable: she can spot an unwashed plate from two rooms away.

definition: To stick firmly to something; to follow a rule or belief.
sentence: I tried to adhere to the diet, but the doughnut adhered more successfully to my hand.

definition: Excessive praise or admiration.
sentence: The puppy received such adulation at the party that he began expecting applause for sitting down.

definition: To publicly support a cause or idea; a person who does so.
sentence: Dad advocates energy conservation while leaving seventeen lights on to search for his glasses.

definition: Concerned with beauty, style, or artistic appearance.
sentence: The café's aesthetic was "rustic farmhouse," which apparently means sitting on a crate beside a mason jar.

definition: Friendly, pleasant, and easy to talk to.
sentence: The affable dentist chatted warmly while holding equipment that looked designed for mining.

definition: To make someone feel isolated, unwelcome, or hostile.
sentence: You can quickly alienate your coworkers by microwaving fish and then asking, "Does anyone smell that?"

definition: A heated argument or confrontation.
sentence: A minor altercation erupted over the last doughnut and required diplomatic intervention from Grandma.

definition: Selflessly concerned with the welfare of others.
sentence: My altruistic brother gave me the last slice of pizza, although I later learned he had already eaten six.

definition: To gather a large amount of something.
sentence: Grandpa amassed so many extension cords that the garage now resembles an electrical octopus preserve.

definition: Open to more than one interpretation; unclear.
sentence: The note "Meet me by the bank" was ambiguous because our town has a river and three financial institutions.

definition: Having mixed or contradictory feelings.
sentence: I was ambivalent about the snowstorm: no school sounded wonderful, but shoveling did not.

definition: To make a bad or difficult situation better.
sentence: We ameliorated the long car ride by giving the children snacks and Grandpa noise-canceling headphones.

definition: Friendly, pleasant, and good-natured.
sentence: The amiable waiter smiled even after my toddler called him "Captain Mustache" for the fifth time.

definition: A state of disorder caused by absence of authority or control.
sentence: When the substitute teacher left for thirty seconds, the classroom descended into anarchy and someone crowned the hamster principal.

definition: Not identified by name.
sentence: An anonymous donor left fifty cupcakes at the office, and productivity immediately became anonymous too.

definition: Hostile, opposing, or unfriendly.
sentence: The cat became antagonistic toward the vacuum after their first meeting and has rejected all peace talks.

definition: Lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern.
sentence: My teenager greeted the announcement of a free museum trip with such apathy that even the couch looked more excited.

definition: To make an earnest request; also to attract or interest.
sentence: The broccoli did not appeal to Leo until I renamed it "tiny edible trees with cheese."

definition: To calm or satisfy someone by meeting a demand.
sentence: We appeased the furious toddler with crackers, stickers, and temporary control of the television remote.

definition: Suitable for growing crops.
sentence: The farmer's arable land produced corn; my backyard mostly produces mysterious plastic toys after snowmelt.

definition: Very old-fashioned or no longer commonly used.
sentence: Dad's archaic phrase "telephone directory" caused the children to assume he meant an app for dinosaurs.

definition: Extremely dry; lacking moisture or interest.
sentence: The desert was arid, and so was Uncle Ted's forty-minute lecture on lawn fertilizer.

definition: Having an exaggerated sense of one's own importance or ability.
sentence: My arrogant rooster appears convinced that sunrise occurs because he personally announces it.

definition: Able to express ideas clearly and effectively; to express clearly.
sentence: The five-year-old was remarkably articulate when explaining why bedtime violated her civil liberties.

definition: An object made by humans, especially one of historical interest.
sentence: The archaeologist found an ancient artifact; my son found a 2007 flip phone and reached the same conclusion.

definition: To move upward or rise.
sentence: I ascended the stairs with dignity until the dog raced past me carrying my sock like a victory flag.

definition: Practicing severe self-discipline and avoiding luxury.
sentence: My ascetic weekend lasted four minutes, ending when I remembered the hotel had room service.

definition: To evaluate or estimate the nature, quality, or value of something.
sentence: The mechanic assessed the strange noise, frowned, and asked whether the car had recently swallowed a trombone.

definition: To make an unpleasant feeling less intense.
sentence: I assuaged my guilt about eating the last cookie by reminding myself that the cookie would have wanted me to be happy.

definition: To waste away or weaken from lack of use.
sentence: My handwriting skills have atrophied so badly that my grocery list now resembles a medical emergency.

definition: Bold or shameless confidence.
sentence: He had the audacity to eat my fries and then complain that I had not ordered enough.

definition: Able to be heard.
sentence: Grandpa's whisper was audible from the driveway and may have altered local migration patterns.

definition: Severely simple, plain, or strict.
sentence: The hotel room was austere: one bed, one chair, and a painting that looked apologetic.

definition: Favoring strict obedience to authority at the expense of personal freedom.
sentence: The toddler ran an authoritarian household in which bedtime was illegal and cookies were compulsory.

definition: A strong dislike or desire to avoid something.
sentence: My cat has an aversion to water, vacuum cleaners, closed doors, and apparently my happiness.

definition: A cause of persistent trouble or distress.
sentence: Autocorrect is the bane of my existence, especially when it turns "meeting" into "meatball."

definition: Unable to produce much vegetation; empty or unproductive.
sentence: The fridge was barren except for mustard, one lime, and a container nobody was brave enough to open.

definition: To make unclear or confused.
sentence: Three hours of contradictory instructions beclouded the issue until nobody remembered what we were assembling.

definition: To give a false impression of; to contradict or disprove.
sentence: His calm smile belied the panic in his eyes as the birthday candles ignited the tablecloth.

definition: Hostile, aggressive, and eager to fight.
sentence: The belligerent goose approached our picnic as though enforcing an unpaid bread tax.

definition: Producing a good or helpful result.
sentence: Exercise is beneficial, which is unfortunate because sitting down is so much more convenient.

definition: Kind, generous, and wishing to do good.
sentence: Our benevolent neighbor returned my runaway dog and included a snack bag for both of us.

definition: An unfair preference for or against something.
sentence: As judge of the pie contest, Grandpa had an obvious bias toward whichever pie was currently on his plate.

definition: A detailed plan or design for how something should be built or achieved.
sentence: My son's blueprint for a treehouse included a waterslide, elevator, and absolutely no discussion of gravity.

definition: To support, strengthen, or reinforce.
sentence: I bolstered my argument for ordering pizza with charts, testimonials, and the fact that I had burned dinner.

definition: To move around energetically and busily.
sentence: Grandma bustled around the kitchen with such speed that the gravy appeared to fear her.

definition: To support or strengthen something.
sentence: The lawyer buttressed his case with photographs, receipts, and one extremely judgmental eyewitness parrot.

definition: A harsh mixture of loud, unpleasant sounds.
sentence: The school band warm-up created a cacophony that caused several nearby birds to reconsider migration.

definition: To persuade someone through flattery or gentle pressure.
sentence: I cajoled the dog off the couch by calling him handsome and mentioning cheese.

definition: Honest, open, and direct expression.
sentence: With refreshing candor, the waiter said, "I work here, and I would not order the fish."

definition: To suppress or remove material considered unacceptable.
sentence: Mom censored Grandpa's wedding toast after discovering the phrase "I probably shouldn't tell this story."

definition: Complete certainty or confidence that something is true.
sentence: Dad announced with certitude that he knew the shortcut, moments before we crossed the same bridge for the third time.

definition: Complete disorder and confusion.
sentence: The kitchen descended into chaos when the mixer started before anyone remembered to attach the bowl.

definition: Continuing for a long time or recurring frequently.
sentence: My chronic habit of losing keys has turned the entryway into an archaeological excavation site.

definition: To limit or restrict within boundaries.
sentence: Mom circumscribed my "small party" to ten guests after I invited the marching band.

definition: Polite and courteous; relating to citizens or nonmilitary matters.
sentence: The siblings remained civil during dinner, which meant nobody threw anything larger than a pea.

definition: Kept secret or done secretly.
sentence: Our clandestine midnight raid on the cookie jar failed when Dad opened the world's loudest bag of chips.

definition: Mercy or lenience, especially in punishment.
sentence: The judge showed clemency and reduced the dog's sentence from "no couch" to "couch with supervision."

definition: To come together and form one whole.
sentence: The children, dog, and Grandma coalesced into a powerful coalition demanding pancakes for dinner.

definition: Logical, clear, and consistent.
sentence: His explanation was coherent until he introduced time travel, a raccoon, and "the cheese factor."

definition: Showing sympathy and concern for others' suffering.
sentence: The compassionate dentist let me choose the music, then politely ignored my request to play funeral marches.

definition: Able to exist or work together without conflict.
sentence: My goals of "sleep late" and "attend the 7 a.m. meeting" were not compatible.

definition: Having sufficient skill or ability to do something well.
sentence: The plumber was competent enough to fix the sink without accidentally improving the toaster.

definition: Able to be understood.
sentence: The directions became comprehensible only after I turned the page right-side up.

definition: Thorough and including nearly everything relevant.
sentence: Dad's comprehensive packing list included sunscreen, passports, and, inexplicably, a rubber chicken.

definition: To admit something is true or to yield after resistance.
sentence: I conceded that Grandma had won the argument after she produced receipts, witnesses, and a labeled pie chart.

definition: To accept or allow behavior considered wrong.
sentence: I do not condone stealing fries, even when the thief is a toddler with excellent negotiation skills.

definition: To keep within limits or a restricted space.
sentence: We confined the puppy to the kitchen, which he interpreted as an invitation to remodel it.

definition: A large, destructive fire.
sentence: One forgotten garlic bread became a conflagration that introduced us to three very friendly firefighters.

definition: To behave according to accepted standards or match a pattern.
sentence: The rebellious sock refused to conform and emerged from the laundry bright pink while all its colleagues were white.

definition: To confuse, surprise, or prove something wrong.
sentence: The new remote confounded Grandpa with forty-seven buttons, three of which appeared to control weather satellites.

definition: To thicken or solidify, especially from cooling.
sentence: The gravy congealed into a substance sturdy enough to support small furniture.

definition: A result or effect of an action or condition.
sentence: The consequence of feeding the dog under the table was discovering he now attends every meal with legal expectations.

definition: Cautious about change; favoring traditional practices or restrained estimates.
sentence: My conservative estimate was that the toddler had spilled "some" cereal; the floor suggested several acres.

definition: To protect from loss or waste; to use sparingly.
sentence: Dad conserves water by taking short showers and then spends twenty minutes explaining that fact.

definition: To combine several things into one stronger or more effective whole.
sentence: We consolidated seven half-empty cereal boxes into one container now known as "Breakfast Roulette."

definition: To make something impure, dirty, or unsafe.
sentence: One red sock contaminated the white laundry and created twelve garments suitable for Valentine's Day.

definition: Existing or occurring in the present time; from the same time period.
sentence: The museum's contemporary art included a chair upside down, which made me reconsider my garage.

definition: A strong feeling that someone or something is worthless or beneath respect.
sentence: The cat regarded the new puppy with the contempt of a duke discovering a goat at dinner.

definition: To become smaller; to enter into a binding agreement; also such an agreement.
sentence: My enthusiasm contracted rapidly after I read the contract and found the phrase "mandatory team-building karaoke."

definition: Following accepted customs or ordinary methods.
sentence: A conventional birthday cake has candles; Uncle Mike's had sparklers, a fog machine, and legal questions.

definition: A firmly held belief; also a formal finding of guilt.
sentence: Grandpa spoke with absolute conviction that the remote was broken, while sitting directly on it.
synonyms: belief; certainty; judgment; finding of guilt

definition: To call people together for a formal meeting.
sentence: The principal convoked an emergency meeting after a goat appeared in the chemistry lab wearing safety goggles.

definition: Large in quantity; abundant.
sentence: The diner served copious fries, enough to settle several international potato disputes.

definition: Warm, friendly, and polite.
sentence: The meeting remained cordial until someone suggested changing Grandma's stuffing recipe.

definition: Dishonest or immoral; to damage or spoil something.
sentence: The corrupt referee accepted a bribe of two cookies and an unusually flattering drawing.

definition: Mysterious or difficult to understand.
sentence: The note on the fridge was cryptic: "Tuesday. Bananas. Trust nobody."

definition: Deserving blame or responsibility for wrongdoing.
sentence: The dog looked culpable because innocent animals rarely hide beneath the table with a whole ham.

definition: To prepare land for crops; to develop a quality, skill, or relationship.
sentence: I cultivated patience by teaching Grandpa how to use streaming television without throwing the remote.

definition: To restrain, control, or limit something.
sentence: I tried to curb my coffee habit by switching to smaller cups and drinking twelve of them.

definition: Quick and not thorough.
sentence: My cursory inspection of the hotel room missed the lizard, which had apparently conducted a much more comprehensive inspection of me.

definition: Distrustful of people's motives and inclined to expect selfishness or disappointment.
sentence: My cynical uncle assumes every "free sample" is merely the opening move in a sophisticated cheese conspiracy.

definition: Seeming difficult enough to cause fear or discouragement.
sentence: The mountain looked daunting until Grandma tightened her shoelaces and asked why everyone was standing around whining.

definition: Fearless and determined despite danger or difficulty.
sentence: The dauntless toddler marched toward the enormous dog armed only with a cracker and unreasonable confidence.

definition: To waste time by moving or acting slowly.
sentence: We told Liam not to dawdle, so he spent ten minutes explaining why he was definitely not dawdling.

definition: To make someone or something weak or less effective.
sentence: The stomach virus debilitated me so thoroughly that lifting the remote felt like competitive weightlifting.

definition: Able to make decisions quickly and firmly; producing a definite result.
sentence: Mom was decisive: either clean the room now or explain to the fire marshal why the floor had disappeared.

definition: Polite, restrained, and appropriate to a formal situation.
sentence: The dinner remained decorous until Grandpa attempted to launch a dinner roll into the bread basket from six feet away.

definition: Proper and polite behavior.
sentence: Restaurant decorum generally discourages sword fighting with breadsticks, a rule my children learned surprisingly late.

definition: To damage someone's reputation by making false statements.
sentence: The squirrel attempted to defame the dog by leaving acorn shells beside the stolen pie.

definition: The act of throwing someone or something out of a window.
sentence: The printer's repeated "paper jam" messages nearly resulted in its defenestration from the second-floor office.

definition: To decline into a worse condition or lower standard.
sentence: The intellectual debate degenerated into two adults shouting, "Your lasagna is weird!"

definition: Done intentionally; or to think carefully before deciding.
sentence: After deliberate consideration, the jury determined that nobody should let Uncle Fred operate the fondue fountain again.

definition: To destroy someone's confidence, spirit, or hope.
sentence: Nothing demoralizes a beginning golfer like watching an eight-year-old casually hit the ball twice as far.

definition: To publicly condemn strongly.
sentence: The neighborhood association denounced the mystery person leaving zucchini on porches, while secretly suspecting Grandma.

definition: To greatly reduce the amount or supply of something.
sentence: One teenage sleepover depleted the refrigerator so completely that the mustard looked lonely.

definition: Copied or developed from something else rather than original.
sentence: The movie felt derivative: it was essentially "Jaws," except the shark was a furious goose.

definition: The complete loss of hope.
sentence: I felt despair when the ice-cream machine displayed "OUT OF ORDER" and the employee nodded with practiced sorrow.

definition: To dislike or hate intensely.
sentence: My cat despises closed doors because they imply a universe in which he is not consulted.

definition: Extremely poor and lacking basic necessities.
sentence: After buying four concert tickets, I felt temporarily destitute and began regarding free ketchup packets as assets.

definition: An indirect route taken to avoid an obstacle or reach a destination.
sentence: Dad's "tiny detour" added forty miles, two tolls, and an unexpected visit to Delaware.

definition: Causing harm or damage.
sentence: Eating nachos during a sit-up contest proved detrimental to both my performance and the gym's upholstery.

definition: Intended to teach, sometimes too obviously or preachily.
sentence: The movie was so didactic that even the villain paused the chase to explain responsible recycling.

definition: A temporary departure from the main subject.
sentence: Grandpa's brief digression about lawn mowers lasted longer than the wedding ceremony.

definition: Showing careful and persistent effort.
sentence: The diligent squirrel moved every birdseed kernel one at a time, unlike me, who postponed unloading the dishwasher until Wednesday.

definition: To make or become smaller, weaker, or less important.
sentence: My confidence diminished when the IKEA instructions introduced a symbol that appeared to mean "summon another adult."

definition: Disagreement or lack of harmony.
sentence: Family discord erupted when someone claimed the superior pizza topping was anchovies.

definition: To harm the reputation of or prove something unworthy of belief.
sentence: The discovery of frosting on his sleeves discredited Ethan's claim that he had never seen the cake.

definition: A feeling that something is unworthy of respect.
sentence: The cat viewed generic tuna with the disdain of a food critic offered a damp napkin.

definition: Annoyed, dissatisfied, and resentful.
sentence: The disgruntled customer demanded a manager because his "bottomless coffee" had, technically, arrived in a cup with a bottom.

definition: A noticeable and often unfair difference between things.
sentence: There was a troubling disparity between my son's definition of "clean room" and every known public-health standard.

definition: To scatter or spread in different directions.
sentence: The crowd dispersed instantly when the organizer announced that cleanup volunteers were needed.

definition: A person's usual mood or temperament; also arrangement or placement.
sentence: The bulldog had a sunny disposition despite having the facial expression of an angry tax auditor.

definition: To spread information or ideas widely.
sentence: Grandma disseminated the family gossip with such efficiency that three cousins knew before the event had actually happened.

definition: To scatter, disappear, or cause something to fade away.
sentence: My motivation to exercise dissipated the moment rain touched the window.

definition: To persuade someone not to do something.
sentence: We tried to dissuade Uncle Bob from buying a unicycle, but the helmet had already arrived.
synonyms: deter; discourage; talk out of; prevent

definition: A variety of different people, things, or qualities.
sentence: The buffet offered impressive diversity: twelve cuisines and one mysterious casserole nobody could geographically identify.

definition: A set of beliefs or principles taught or held by a group.
sentence: Dad's household doctrine is simple: never pay full price and never trust a printer.

definition: To record information or evidence in detail; also a written record.
sentence: My sister documented the dog's crimes with forty-seven photographs and a spreadsheet titled "Sock Incidents."

definition: Expressing beliefs as unquestionably true and refusing other views.
sentence: My uncle is dogmatic about barbecue: there is one correct sauce, and apparently dissent is punishable by exile.

definition: Inactive for a period but capable of becoming active again.
sentence: My exercise routine has been dormant since January but remains theoretically alive.

definition: Stern, gloomy, and unfriendly in appearance or manner.
sentence: The dour waiter looked at our birthday hats as though happiness required a permit.

definition: Doubtful, questionable, or uncertain.
sentence: The dog's claim that "the cat did it" seemed dubious because the cat weighs eight pounds and the turkey weighed fifteen.

definition: Unconventional or oddly distinctive in behavior.
sentence: Our eccentric neighbor walks his pet duck in a stroller and refers to Tuesdays as "formalwear day."

definition: Lively, bubbly, and enthusiastic; also fizzy.
sentence: Her effervescent personality was so cheerful at 7 a.m. that several coworkers suspected witchcraft.

definition: Elicit means to draw out a response; illicit means illegal or forbidden.
sentence: The teacher tried to elicit an answer, not arrange an illicit shipment of algebra worksheets across state lines.

definition: Fluent, persuasive, and graceful in expression.
sentence: The toddler gave an eloquent defense of eating cookies for breakfast, citing happiness, efficiency, and constitutional precedent.

definition: To make something clear by explaining it.
sentence: The mechanic elucidated the problem by saying, "This part should not be smoking."

definition: Difficult to find, catch, understand, or achieve.
sentence: A clean kitchen was elusive because every time I finished, another child appeared holding peanut butter.

definition: To decorate or add details, sometimes exaggerated ones.
sentence: Grandpa embellished the fishing story until the trout had a name, a college degree, and legal representation.

definition: To accept enthusiastically; also to hold someone closely.
sentence: I embraced minimalism by throwing away one magazine and then celebrating with three new storage baskets.

definition: To publicly approve or support something.
sentence: The dog enthusiastically endorsed the new household policy permitting bacon on Sundays.

definition: To suffer through or continue despite difficulty.
sentence: I endured the six-hour recital with dignity, snacks, and a rapidly declining phone battery.

definition: Interesting, charming, or pleasant enough to hold attention.
sentence: The professor was engaging enough to make tax law sound like a mildly dangerous adventure.

definition: To cause or give rise to something.
sentence: The phrase "mandatory Saturday meeting" engendered immediate sadness throughout the office.

definition: To improve or increase the quality, value, or attractiveness of something.
sentence: A little parsley enhanced the soup; the plastic googly eyes did not.

definition: To give someone greater knowledge or understanding.
sentence: My teenager enlightened me on current slang and then asked me never to use any of it publicly.

definition: To involve something as a necessary result or requirement.
sentence: Owning a puppy entails walks, vet bills, and accepting that one shoe will always be mysteriously damp.

definition: To twist together or involve in a complicated situation.
sentence: My headphones became entangled in my pocket with enough complexity to qualify as nautical rigging.

definition: Lasting for a very short time.
sentence: My resolve to avoid dessert was ephemeral; it vanished when the crème brûlée arrived.

definition: Unpredictable and inconsistent in behavior or movement.
sentence: The squirrel's erratic path across the road resembled someone trying to choose a checkout line.

definition: Having or showing extensive knowledge.
sentence: The erudite professor quoted Plato, Shakespeare, and, unexpectedly, a 1980s cereal commercial.

definition: Intended for or understood by only a small group with specialized knowledge.
sentence: The board game's rules were so esoteric that the inventor had to call his mother for clarification.

definition: Respect and admiration; to regard highly.
sentence: I hold Grandma in great esteem, particularly when she is standing near a tray of brownies.

definition: To cause someone to become distant or unfriendly.
sentence: Serving decaf without warning may estrange you from certain members of my family permanently.

definition: To leave someone or something out.
sentence: The club excluded anyone unwilling to wear the ceremonial lobster hat, which dramatically reduced membership.

definition: To clear someone from blame or guilt.
sentence: The security camera exonerated the toddler and revealed that Grandpa had eaten the missing cupcake.

definition: To make a process happen faster.
sentence: Offering pizza expedited the meeting more effectively than any management consultant in company history.

definition: Clearly and directly stated, leaving no ambiguity.
sentence: Mom's instructions were explicit: "Do not put the hamster in the dishwasher," a sentence she had not expected to need.

definition: To praise enthusiastically and highly.
sentence: Grandpa extolled the virtues of his new recliner as though it had won a Nobel Prize.

definition: Spending or using more than is necessary; excessively elaborate.
sentence: The extravagant birthday cake had six tiers, edible gold, and its own lighting technician.

definition: To free someone or something from a difficult or tangled situation.
sentence: We extricated Dad from the folding lawn chair after first agreeing never to discuss the incident again.

definition: To make an action or process easier.
sentence: The teacher used snacks to facilitate discussion, accidentally proving that granola bars can improve democracy.

definition: Very careful about cleanliness, detail, or correctness.
sentence: The fastidious cat refused to drink from his bowl because one hair was floating in it—his own.

definition: Able to produce abundant crops or offspring; productive in ideas.
sentence: My nephew has a fertile imagination in which every missing sock is evidence of an underground civilization.

definition: Intense passion or enthusiasm.
sentence: Dad defended his preferred brand of charcoal with the fervor of a revolutionary pamphleteer.

definition: Skillful handling of a delicate situation.
sentence: With impressive finesse, Grandma changed the subject just before Uncle Ted began discussing politics at Thanksgiving.

definition: Obviously and shockingly wrong or offensive.
sentence: The dog's flagrant theft of the sandwich occurred in full view of six witnesses and one security camera.

definition: To grow or develop successfully; to thrive.
sentence: The basil flourished after I stopped "helping" it and let Grandma take over.

definition: Happening by chance, often with a fortunate result.
sentence: It was fortuitous that I missed my train because the next platform had a doughnut shop.

definition: Lucky or favored by good circumstances.
sentence: I was fortunate to find my lost wallet before the dog discovered its leather-based culinary potential.

definition: Physically weak, delicate, or easily damaged.
sentence: The frail antique chair survived 120 years and then met my cousin after Thanksgiving dinner.

definition: Open, honest, and direct.
sentence: The doctor was frank: "You need more exercise, and carrying snacks upstairs does not count."

definition: Basic, essential, or forming a necessary foundation.
sentence: A fundamental rule of family travel is that someone will need the bathroom five minutes after departure.

definition: To gather, earn, or collect.
sentence: The puppy garnered more applause for sneezing than I did for completing my entire presentation.

definition: Dizzy or wildly excited.
sentence: I became giddy when the waiter said "unlimited breadsticks," which may reveal too much about my ambitions.

definition: To dig or cut deeply; also to charge an unfairly high price.
sentence: The stadium gouged me twelve dollars for water, so I briefly considered drinking from the decorative fountain.

definition: To give or formally allow something requested.
sentence: After lengthy negotiations, Mom granted the children permission to stay up an extra eleven minutes.

definition: Vividly detailed, especially in a way that is striking or disturbing; also visual.
sentence: Grandpa gave a graphic description of his knee surgery just as the appetizers arrived.

definition: To satisfy or please a desire or person.
sentence: It gratified me enormously when the cat finally chose my lap, until I realized I was sitting beside the tuna.

definition: Giving pleasure, satisfaction, or a sense of achievement.
sentence: It was gratifying to finish the puzzle, especially after three days of accusing the manufacturer of hiding a piece.

definition: Sociable and fond of company.
sentence: The gregarious golden retriever greeted every person at the park as a long-lost business partner.

definition: Too easily persuaded to believe something.
sentence: My gullible cousin believed me when I said the elevator required a password and spent five minutes guessing.

definition: To hinder or obstruct progress.
sentence: My attempt to cook dinner was hampered by the smoke alarm's relentless criticism.

definition: The belief that pleasure is a primary or important goal of life.
sentence: My weekend hedonism consisted of pancakes, pajamas, and refusing to acknowledge the existence of errands.

definition: Boisterous laughter or great amusement.
sentence: Hilarity erupted when Dad discovered he had worn one slipper and one dress shoe to the restaurant.

definition: To make progress difficult or slow.
sentence: The toddler hindered our packing by removing every item from the suitcase as soon as we put it in.

definition: Of the same kind or type throughout; often used similarly to homogeneous.
sentence: The committee was so homogenous that all six members arrived wearing nearly identical blue sweaters.

definition: Modest about one's importance or ability; not grand or luxurious.
sentence: Despite winning the spelling bee, Maya remained humble and only wore her medal to breakfast, lunch, and dinner.

definition: A modest view of one's own importance or abilities.
sentence: Dad showed admirable humility by admitting the GPS had been right for the first 173 miles.

definition: To use or manage resources carefully and economically.
sentence: Grandpa husbands paper towels so carefully that one sheet can apparently survive an entire weekend.

definition: A person who claims moral standards or beliefs that their own behavior contradicts.
sentence: My brother called me a hypocrite for banning snacks in the car while eating pretzels at a red light.

definition: A proposed explanation that can be tested or investigated.
sentence: My hypothesis was that the dog ate the homework; the shredded algebra sheet in his bed strengthened the theory.

definition: Illegal, forbidden, or not permitted.
sentence: The children operated an illicit candy exchange behind the sofa with pricing sophisticated enough to alarm economists.

definition: To light up; to make something clearer or easier to understand.
sentence: The flashlight illuminated the basement and, unfortunately, the enormous spider we had been happier not understanding.

definition: Fair and not favoring one side over another.
sentence: We chose Grandma as an impartial judge of the pie contest, forgetting that she had baked one of the pies.

definition: To slow, block, or obstruct progress.
sentence: My progress down the hallway was impeded by a cat lying sideways with the confidence of a fallen tree.

definition: Unable to be upset, disturbed, or excited easily.
sentence: The imperturbable flight attendant smiled calmly while a passenger tried to store a cello in the overhead bin.

definition: To force something unwelcome or burdensome on someone.
sentence: Uncle Ted imposed his vacation slideshow on us with the grim efficiency of a tax audit.

definition: Acting suddenly without careful thought.
sentence: In an impulsive moment, I bought a kayak despite living nowhere near water.

definition: The beginning or starting point of something.
sentence: From its inception, the family group chat was doomed by Grandpa discovering GIFs.

definition: A tendency, preference, or slope.
sentence: My natural inclination is to exercise in the morning, provided "exercise" means turning over and "morning" means noon.

definition: Including a wide range of people or things and not excluding relevant groups.
sentence: The picnic was inclusive: children, grandparents, dogs, and one squirrel who contributed nothing financially.

definition: Out of place or not matching its surroundings.
sentence: The pink flamingo looked incongruous in the solemn boardroom, especially because someone had given it a tie.

definition: To include something as part of a whole.
sentence: I incorporated vegetables into dinner by putting one parsley leaf beside the pizza.

definition: Unable to be tired out; persistently energetic.
sentence: The indefatigable toddler asked "why?" for three straight hours while every adult visibly aged.

definition: Having no particular interest, sympathy, or preference.
